uncited: Physical Attribute Computation generates secondary volumetric fields (such as velocity, size, or distance) from primary data (intensity, geometry, or segmentation) to enhance Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) or fluid simulation.

It differs from siblings like [Interior Voxelize](995-interior-voxelize.md) or [Box-filtering Density Estimation](5987-box-filtering-density-estimation.md) by computing derived physical properties rather than raw density or occupancy, and from [Multi-pattern Volumetric Construction via Voxel Multiplication](8874-multi-pattern-volumetric-construction-via-voxel-multiplicati.md) by focusing on attribute derivation rather than pattern composition.
A volumetric attribute not directly derived from intensity, but calculated on pre-segmented parts of a volume.
The concept of using attributes beyond intensity for visualization was explored in the context of transfer functions.

Correa and Ma (2008) adapted the concept of "size" to Direct Volume Rendering, noting the difficulty in defining mathematical descriptors for size variations in multiscale fields, similar to challenges in Computer Vision .
